summary: Onset was ~06:49-06:50Z. Load on the auth-service login path rose ~4x (request_rate ~395 -> ~1500 req/s) while every other backend stayed flat, and auth-service CPU pinned at ~97% with its worker pool saturated (64/64, queue up to ~98k) and 503s ("accept queue full") on POST /v1/auth/login only. The HPA repeatedly wanted 14 replicas but was capped at maxReplicas 8, so it could not scale into the surge. There was NO auth-service deployment in the window (last deploy window empty, only an unrelated portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 05:50), NO relevant config change (only log.level INFO->WARN at 03:40), and NO degraded dependency (redis hit_ratio steady 96%, user-db CPU 18% with flat slow queries). The report's "bcrypt regression" hypothesis is contradicted: a code regression needs a release, and none occurred; the signature is demand exceeding provisioned capacity on a workload (login) that is CPU-expensive. Root cause: capacity saturation of auth-service — login traffic outgrew the provisioned replica ceiling (maxReplicas=8), causing CPU saturation, worker-pool/accept-queue exhaustion, latency ~3.8s and 503s. Whether the extra login traffic is organic or a stuffing/retry burst is a data gap, but the fault originates at auth-service's provisioning ceiling.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation: login traffic outgrew auth-service's replica ceiling
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Login-path load on auth-service rose ~4x at 06:49Z (request_rate ~395 -> ~1500 req/s) with no code or config change. Because login is CPU-intensive, auth-service CPU pinned ~97%, worker pool saturated (64/64, queue to ~98k) and the accept queue filled, producing ~3.8s latency and 503s on POST /v1/auth/login. The HPA could not absorb the surge because it was capped at maxReplicas 8 (it wanted 14). Downstream (redis, user-db) stayed healthy, so the fault originates in auth-service provisioning.

causal_chain.claim: Login request rate rises ~4x (~395 -> ~1500 req/s) at 06:49Z
auth-service CPU saturates to ~97% and worker pool / accept queue exhaust
Latency rises to ~3.8s and login returns 503
HPA cannot scale past maxReplicas 8 (wanted 14), so saturation persists

assumptions: The 4x request-rate increase reflects real inbound login demand (organic surge or stuffing/attack) rather than a metrics artifact.
Login handling is CPU-bound such that 4x rate saturates the 8-replica ceiling.

ranked_hypotheses.title: bcrypt/code regression in a recent auth-service release (report's hypothesis)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A recent auth-service release raised the bcrypt cost factor (as in HIST-101), making each login far more CPU-expensive and causing 4s latency and 503s.

causal_chain.claim: bad auth-service release raises bcrypt cost

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No auth-service deployment exists in the window (count 0 over Apr 1-22); a code regression requires a release. Also, CPU/latency rose in lockstep with a 4x request-rate increase rather than per-request cost rising at constant load, and dependencies are healthy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Dependency failure (redis-cache or user-db) cascading into auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared datastore degraded, slowing auth-service logins and causing timeouts/503s.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: redis hit_ratio steady ~96% with no CPU rise, and user-db CPU flat ~18% with flat slow queries; neither dependency shows degradation at onset. Errors are accept-queue/worker-pool saturation, not DB/cache timeouts.

facts.statement: auth-service p99 rose from ~90ms to ~3800ms and error_rate from ~0.2% to ~14% at the 06:50 onset.
auth-service request rate rose ~4x (from ~395 to ~1500 req/s) at onset with no code or config change.
auth-service CPU pinned at ~97%; worker pool saturated (64/64, queue to ~98k); 503 'accept queue full' on login.
auth-service autoscaler wanted 14 replicas but was capped at maxReplicas 8 throughout the incident.
api-gateway traffic rose ~4x but its CPU stayed flat (~42%); all other backends were flat.
Dependencies were healthy at onset: redis hit_ratio ~96%, user-db CPU ~18% with flat slow queries.
No auth-service deployment occurred in the incident window; only an unrelated portfolio-service deploy at 05:50.

assumptions: The 4x request-rate rise reflects real inbound demand on the login path rather than a metrics/scrape artifact.
auth-service login handling is CPU-bound (e.g. password hashing), so a 4x rate saturates the 8-replica ceiling.
Multiple/HA auth-service replicas exist behind the worker-pool metric, so raising the replica cap is a valid mitigation.

timeline.event: auth-service config change log.level INFO->WARN (cfg-2801) — unrelated to request handling.
auth-service 'config reloaded (no changes)' — just before onset.
auth-service request_rate ~4x, CPU ~97%, p99 ~3.8s, error_rate ~14% all begin (06:50 bucket).
Autoscaler reports desired 14 > maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further.
Reported_at: on-call SRE reports login latency/503s.
Incident still ongoing at latest data: p99 ~3.8s, error_rate ~14%, CPU ~97%, HPA still capped.

recommended_actions.action: Raise auth-service HPA maxReplicas (currently 8) to at least 14-16 so it can scale into the login surge, and add capacity headroom (or a floor above current steady state).
recommended_actions.rationale: The autoscaler wanted 14 replicas but was capped at 8 the entire incident; scaling is the direct relief for CPU/worker-pool saturation.

recommended_actions.action: Protect the login endpoint: rate-limit / add bot/credential-stuffing defenses or per-client throttling on POST /v1/auth/login so a login flood cannot saturate auth-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: All errors are confined to the login endpoint and load rose 4x only there; if this is a stuffing/retry burst, throttling cuts demand at the source.

recommended_actions.action: Verify whether the 4x login surge is organic, a retry storm from api-gateway, or an attack (check gateway egress/client mix and auth login failure sources) before treating as pure capacity.
recommended_actions.rationale: Distinguishes capacity_saturation from an abusive-traffic data_issue and determines the durable fix; gateway request_rate exceeds the sum of backend rates.

recommended_actions.action: Add pre-scaling for known demand peaks and alerting on HPA hitting maxReplicas and on accept-queue saturation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Historical analog HIST-113 shows a repeated pattern of provisioned capacity being exceeded; earlier detection/prescale prevents recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back or revert auth-service code: there was no auth-service release; the report's bcrypt-regression hypothesis is unsupported.
recommended_actions.rationale: No deployment exists in the window, so a rollback has no target and would not address a load-driven saturation.

data_gaps: Source of the 4x login surge is unverified: no per-client/IP/attack telemetry or gateway client-mix data was available, so organic surge vs. credential-stuffing vs. retry loop cannot be separated.
api-gateway INFO/WARN logs for auth requests returned 0 matches (only 2 generic 'connection reset' retries), so a gateway-side retry-amplification loop cannot be fully ruled out.
kyc-provider (external, auth-service downstream) and bank-partner-api have no telemetry, so an external-provider contribution to login latency cannot be excluded from telemetry.
No replica-count or per-pod CPU timeseries for auth-service was available; the maxReplicas=8 cap is inferred from autoscaler warnings rather than a scaling config read.

findings.statement: auth-service p99 latency rose from ~90ms (through 06:40) to ~2288ms in the 06:50 bucket and stayed ~3800ms thereafter.
auth-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% (through 06:40) to 7.11% in the 06:50 bucket and settled ~14% afterwards.
auth-service request_rate rose from a steady ~395 req/s (through 06:45) to ~1490 req/s from 07:00 onward, i.e. roughly a 4x increase.
auth-service CPU rose from ~38% to ~97% at the same 06:50 onset and stayed pinned near 97%.
auth-service logs show worker pool saturation (active=64/64, queue up to 98763) and 503s 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' starting 06:54:53/06:55:42.

refs.quote: request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)

findings.statement: auth-service autoscaler repeatedly reports wanting more replicas than allowed: 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' (34 occurrences, 06:57-08:58).

refs.quote: autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further

findings.statement: api-gateway request_rate also rose ~4x at 06:50 (from ~1250 to ~4900 req/s) while its CPU stayed flat at ~42%, i.e. the gateway was not the bottleneck.
Other backends behind the gateway were flat across the onset: order-service (~230 req/s), market-data-service (~945), portfolio-service (~570), payment-service (~100) all unchanged.
No auth-service deployment occurred in the incident window (get_deployments for auth-service over 2026-04-01..04-22 returned count 0); the only deploy was portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 05:50.
The only config change in the window was auth-service log.level INFO->WARN at 03:40 (cfg-2801), which is unrelated to request handling; no api-gateway config changes.
Dependencies showed no degradation: redis-cache hit_ratio steady ~96% (no cold-cache storm), user-db CPU flat ~18% with slow_queries_per_min flat ~0.3, redis CPU ~22%.
user-db connections_active rose from ~25 to ~80 at onset (06:48 bucket onward), consistent with more login work reaching the DB, but without slow queries or CPU pressure.
All auth-service errors were confined to the login endpoint: querying '/v1/auth/' returned only 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' (372 matches).

refs.quote: request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)

findings.statement: The fault is demand exceeding auth-service's provisioned replica ceiling, not a code/config/dependency fault: load spiked 4x on the CPU-expensive login path, CPU pinned at 97%, and the HPA was capped at maxReplicas 8 — a signature consistent with capacity saturation, and analogous to past incident HIST-113 ('Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity').
